$comment: Every lint escape in shipped code (packages/*/src, except vendored code). scripts/check-type-escapes.ts fails on any escape not listed here, and on any entry that no longer matches. Add one only when no typed alternative exists, with the reason.

allowed.reason: KmsKeyConfig is an open union that third-party providers extend by augmentation, which TypeScript cannot see from the core.
The same open-union cast as above: a single `as` is rejected (TS2352) because no member of the closed union overlaps a third-party key.

For a schema known only at run time, the encoder's type says every field is a nested struct, so no real payload fits it; the encoder validates the payload itself, and the result also feeds micro-eth-signer's verifyTyped.
The debug output escapes control characters, so the pattern has to match them.
The plugin's one warning helper prints for the user, as Hardhat plugins print warnings: KMS keys on the default network, and EIP-7702 authorizations that nodes would skip.
--kms reads Foundry's environment variables directly, as decision 0008 records.
isConfigurationVariable checks Hardhat's `_type` marker; hasEveryPart checks that every part has a string value, so mapParts needs no cast.
isObject checks for a non-null object, for zod's conditional unions.
isRecord and isField check the shape parseTypedData relies on, field by field.
assertAdapter runs the adapter contract checks (describe(), signing and identity methods) before the adapter is used.

AZURE_CLIENT_ID selects a user-assigned managed identity. ManagedIdentityCredential does not read it itself; only DefaultAzureCredential does, and DefaultAzureCredential tries its sources in another order than Foundry's. The explicit chain therefore reads it and passes it on.
